purpose: Original material-selection guides informed by competitor content gaps, with technical facts checked against manufacturer and trade sources. Public content does not establish ranking causation.

findings.observedPattern: Separates porcelain, ceramic and other material categories, then links selection and cost guidance into a visible installation process.
findings.limitation: Used only for information architecture and selection topics. Public page content does not establish why it ranks; no brand stock, showroom or guarantees transferred.

findings.observedPattern: Connects tile choices, pattern options and the intended surface with service navigation.
findings.limitation: No countertop offering, ratings, credentials or project claims adopted. Tiling.ca material pages remain editorial guides rather than product inventories.

findings.observedPattern: Defines ceramic as a broad clay-based category and porcelain as a denser subtype; distinguishes intended use and finish considerations.
findings.limitation: Avoided promotional universal best/durability claims and all numerical friction/size thresholds. Exact product approval governs suitability.

findings.observedPattern: Explains the material relationship and differences useful when comparing product choices.
findings.limitation: No claim that all products in either category share the same approved uses, performance or price.

findings.observedPattern: Uses application-specific selection for backsplashes and shower walls and refers customers to each product’s suitability information.
findings.limitation: Did not reuse sweeping waterproof, resale-value or same-day installation claims; wet-wall suitability remains conditional and separate from waterproofing.

findings.observedPattern: Care varies for surface types; guidance includes residue removal, small-area testing and specific protective-treatment advice for some polished porcelain.
findings.limitation: Daltile’s polished-porcelain guidance differs from broad no-sealer wording at other manufacturers. Draft directs readers to the exact product and separates grout; no universal no-sealer rule.

findings.observedPattern: Distinguishes tile surfaces, routine dirt removal, compatible cleaners and grout considerations.
findings.limitation: Manufacturer-specific instructions are not extended to every decorative finish. No acid-cleaning recipe, blanket sealer recommendation or treatment frequency copied.

findings.observedPattern: Explains mechanical edge finishing and dimensional consistency of rectified tile while still specifying grout joints.
findings.limitation: No manufacturer-specific joint-width figure copied; layout and joints remain dependent on exact product and installation requirements.

findings.source: Ceramic Tile Education Foundation — homeowner guide
findings.observedPattern: Recommends seeing multiple pieces, approving variation and mockups, and confirming compatibility through product data sheets.
findings.limitation: No certification implication, numerical installation standard or legal recommendation adopted. Original customer checklist addresses selection decisions.

findings.observedPattern: Shows intentional variation in handmade and handmade-look decorative tile.
findings.limitation: A style label is not evidence that any delivered defect is acceptable; draft advises comparing real pieces with approved samples before installation.

findings.observedPattern: Distinguishes tile and grout finishes from the shower’s waterproofing system.
findings.limitation: General assembly distinction only; no named-brand installation offering or universal system specified.

findings.source: Prime Tiling — natural marble versus marble-look porcelain
findings.observedPattern: A dedicated material comparison answers a real selection decision. Original Tiling.ca copy separates natural stone from manufactured stone-look finishes and makes care, sample review and intended use explicit.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. Used the comparison structure only, not claims of value, lifespan, relative luxury, price or blanket durability. No ranking causation inferred.

findings.observedPattern: Material-specific sections and room-selection FAQs make it easier to move from a material name to an installation decision. Tiling.ca content now links potential applications to its existing service and pricing pages.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. Competitor performance generalizations and universally suitable room/material claims were not adopted.

findings.observedPattern: Natural stone is distinguished from standard tile pricing, with the stone and substrate reviewed together. This informed explicit product/application details and quantity/installation questions instead of presenting a single generic stone package.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. Competitor prices, inventory, in-home samples, free measures and scheduling promises are not Tiling.ca offerings and were not copied.

findings.source: Natural Stone Institute — Care & Cleaning of Natural Stone
findings.observedPattern: Primary trade guidance supports stone identification, neutral cleaning, abrasive-grit control, product-specific sealing and the limit that sealing improves resistance rather than making stone stain-proof.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. Generic care does not establish the suitability, sealing need or maintenance interval of an individual supplied product. No chemical recipes or restoration procedures reproduced.

findings.source: LATICRETE — Stone and Tile Care Guide
findings.observedPattern: Manufacturer guidance distinguishes acid etching from staining and explains that sealing cannot stop acid etching. Supports marble care boundaries without promising polishing or restoration.
findings.limitation: Read 2026-11-08; this is an older regional technical sheet. Only stable general care distinctions used. No named product endorsement, availability or application specification inferred; current selected-product instructions govern.

findings.observedPattern: Manufacturer recommends neutral stone-compatible cleaning and makes acid sensitivity, treatment effects and refinishing distinct issues. Supports material-specific care and checking a treatment’s appearance before use.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. Did not generalize Daltile’s blanket sealing advice or suggested interval to every stone. No product catalogue, brand supply or restoration service promise added.

findings.source: Natural Stone Institute / Use Natural Stone — Travertine
findings.observedPattern: Explains travertine’s porous texture and the choice of filled versus unfilled surfaces. Used to prompt confirmation of filling, finish and maintenance in the stone selection.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. No universal use approval, hardness threshold or sealing frequency inferred.

findings.source: Natural Stone Institute / Use Natural Stone — Slate
findings.observedPattern: Explains the slightly irregular cleft surface commonly seen in slate tile. Supports reviewing texture and representative pieces rather than treating all slate as a uniform smooth finish.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. Promotional durability, low-maintenance and other blanket claims were not adopted; wet/exterior suitability remains product-specific.

findings.source: Natural Stone Institute / Use Natural Stone — Selecting the Ideal Stone Finish
findings.observedPattern: Distinguishes reflective polished, matte honed and textured stone finishes. Supports viewing the actual finish and colour under intended lighting.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. No universal traction or exterior approval is assigned to a finish name. Countertop examples are not represented as Tiling.ca countertop services.

findings.source: Natural Stone Institute / Use Natural Stone — A Scientific Guide to Shopping for Natural Stone
findings.observedPattern: Primary trade publication explains acid sensitivity of marble, limestone and travertine compared with typical granite. Supports a concrete care comparison while preserving product-specific limits and avoiding immunity claims.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. No destructive sample-testing instructions, numerical properties or refinishing promises reproduced. General classification does not verify a particular supplied product.

findings.source: Natural Stone Institute / Use Natural Stone — Limestone
findings.observedPattern: Primary geological overview describes limestone variation, including fossil detail. Used only to prompt examination of the actual pieces rather than promise a uniform appearance.
findings.limitation: Checked 2026-11-08. Named quarry products, structural properties and exterior suitability are not generalized to all limestone tile.

implementation: Five bilingual material guides and comparison hub
Exact-product use/finish/care distinctions; marble and granite correctly treated as natural stone
Relevant service/pricing links; general benchmarks not presented as material-specific prices
Validated material, service and city context in primary quote journeys
Article and visible FAQ schema, not inventory/Product/Offer claims
